summary: Sporting News tracker of Shohei Ohtani's 2023 free agency, running from Nov. 30 to Dec. 9. It logs reports on finalists (Dodgers, Cubs, Blue Jays, Angels, Giants, Braves), contract expectations, and conflicting Blue Jays rumors, ending with Ohtani agreeing to a 10-year, $700 million deal with the Dodgers.
one_line: Rolling tracker of Shohei Ohtani's 2023 free agency rumors, ending with his 10-year, $700 million agreement with the Dodgers on Dec. 9.
key_facts: Shohei Ohtani announced Saturday, Dec. 9 that he agreed to a 10-year, $700 million contract with the Dodgers, which includes "significant deferrals."
Because of the deferrals, the Dodgers will not pay Ohtani $70 million per year and will pay him beyond the 10 seasons.
The Dodgers pair Ohtani, a two-time MVP, with former MVPs Mookie Betts and Freddie Freeman.
On Dec. 8, J.P. Hoornstra of Dodgers Nation reported Ohtani picked the Blue Jays, but Ben Nicholson-Smith of Sportsnet said no decision had been made.
Jon Morosi reported Ohtani was headed to Toronto on Dec. 8, but Bob Nightengale and Nicholson-Smith then reported he was at his home in Southern California.
Ohtani originally signed with the Angels on Dec. 8, 2017, six years before the Dec. 8, 2023 decision rumors.
Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said the team met with Ohtani for 2-3 hours over the weekend and called him "clearly" the top priority.
On Dec. 5, Bob Nightengale reported Cubs optimism had "significantly wanted" (sic), leaving the Dodgers, Blue Jays, Angels and Giants as finalists.
Ken Rosenthal reported Ohtani was believed to have met the Blue Jays at their Florida complex on Dec. 4, away from the winter meetings in Nashville.
Jon Heyman reported on Dec. 3 that Ohtani had received several offers above $500 million, with five teams in the running.
On Dec. 1, Jeff Passan reported the Rangers, Red Sox and Mets appeared out, and Ohtani expected $550-$600 million.
Jon Morosi reported the Braves were "engaged" with Ohtani's camp on Dec. 4.
Mike Trout's record deal is 12 years, $426.5 million.
Jon Heyman reported rivals believed Bo Bichette and Vladimir Guerrero Jr., both free agents after 2025, could be traded if Toronto signed Ohtani.
